key_factors: AFCON 2025 champions — Morocco arrive with tournament-winning mentality and genuine belief
Loss of Aguerd (CB) and Ezzalzouli (winger) announced just days before — huge disruption
Counter-attacking identity from Qatar 2022 remains: unbeaten in all matches with under 50% possession
Brazil's own injury crisis (Neymar, Rodrygo, Estêvão out) removes their biggest attacking threats
New coach Ouahbi — limited time to embed his system adds uncertainty for Morocco
reasoning: Morocco come in as African champions with real tournament momentum, but the Aguerd and Ezzalzouli injuries couldn't have arrived at a worse time. Facing Vinicius Jr without their first-choice CB is a daunting prospect even for the best-organised low-block. Morocco's best hope: defend deep, stay compact, and use Brahim Díaz and transitions to threaten a Brazil midfield that may lack cohesion without Neymar pulling the strings. A goal is realistic; an equaliser possible. But winning against Brazil, even this injury-hit version, is asking too much. Morocco expect a narrow defeat and will target Scotland and Haiti for their points.

Morocco's defensive organisation, AFCON 2025 championship pedigree, and Hakimi's attacking threat from right-back mean this is far from a Brazil procession. The losses of Aguerd and Ezzalzouli hurt but do not erase Morocco's identity: hard to break down, lethal on the counter. Brazil will score — likely through Vinícius — but Brahim Díaz or El Khannouss will find a way through. Morocco hold firm for a 1-1 draw, earning a historic opening-match point against the Seleção.

summary: Morocco's defensive discipline and counter-attacking threat neutralise an injury-hit Brazil. A Vinícius goal is cancelled out by Brahim Díaz as the Atlas Lions earn a hard-fought, tactically brilliant draw.
